title: Signed API key timestamp drift causing intermittent tenant authorization denials
creator: Amina Patel
description: Production customers across Hosted and Dedicated started seeing intermittent 401/403s for well-formed signed API keys after a scheduled keystore rolling swap. The errors surface as tenant scoping denials (token not bound to tenant) for requests that previously succeeded. Issue first reported by two enterprise customers with Dedicated instances and one hosted account on 2026-03-04.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Configure an API key that uses signed tokens tied to tenant metadata.
2) Initiate a rolling keystore swap on a multi-node dedicated pool (simulate by rotating signing key on half the nodes, then the other half).
3) Send concurrent requests that reuse long-lived client connections / keep-alive and observe intermittent 401/403s during the swap window.
4) Reproduction is more likely with sustained parallel traffic and with edge proxy in front of runtime.
observed_symptoms: Intermittent 401 (unauthorized) or 403 (forbidden) for valid API keys
Errors correlate to a 30-90s window around keystore rotations
Affected requests often reuse the same TCP connection; new connections after rotation succeed consistently
Logs show a signature verification pass on runtime node A but tenant lookup fails when token is resolved against node B's ephemeral cache
root_cause: Race between key rotation propagation and runtime tenant-binding cache invalidation. Signed API keys include a timestamp signature tied to a key ID. During rolling swaps, some front-end nodes accepted tokens signed by new key while backend runtime nodes still had stale tenant->key binding in cache, causing a tenant-scoped lookup to fail. Additionally, edge proxy connection reuse caused requests to land on different backends mid-swap, exposing the inconsistency.
mitigation: 1) Hotfixed runtime to fall back to a short verification path that accepts either the old or new key for tokens within a 2-minute grace window. 2) Temporarily disabled aggressive connection reuse on the edge proxy for affected customers. 3) Replayed an immediate full invalidation of tenant binding caches post-rotation to reduce drift.
resolution_plan:
Short term: ship hotfix (runtime-2.3.1-hotfix) to add key-grace verification and cache invalidation hook (ETA: 2026-03-10). Roll out to Hosted within one hour of release. For Dedicated, provide a staged patch and runbook for operators to coordinate rotation safely (ETA: 2026-03-12).

Long term: implement a coordinated rotation protocol: (a) preflight announcement to all routing and runtime nodes, (b) synchronized cache flush barrier after key swap, (c) metric and alerting change to detect signed-key mismatch rate. Also add an automated safety fallback that pins routing to nodes with compatible key state during rotations.
tradeoffs_discussed:
- Extending the verification grace window increases risk surface if keys are compromised (mitigated by narrow time window and audit logs).
- Forcing connection draining on edge proxies increases short-term latency and operational overhead but reduces customer errors.
- Coordinated rotation protocol adds complexity to keystore service but prevents future customer-impacting races.
commits: runtime: add fallback key verification and cache invalidation hook (commit: a1b2c3d)
edge-proxy: add option to disable connection pooling during rotations (commit: f4e5d6a)
ops: runbook and automation for coordinated rotations (commit: 3f7a2b1)
monitoring_and_alerting: Added a new metric: auth.signed_key_mismatch.rate and alert when >0.5% of requests in 5m window. Instrumented tenant-binding cache misses correlated to rotation_id. Dashboard panels added to runtime and edge team views.
post_mortem_actions: 1) Complete coordinated rotation protocol design and land RFC (owner: Security Infra)
2) Add e2e test that exercises rolling keystore swap with connection reuse enabled (owner: QA)
3) Add a migration-safe validation step in the keystore service that enforces cache invalidation fences (owner: Runtime)
